requirement: A struct can contain data members.
A struct can contain function members.
A struct is a value type.
Struct values do not require heap allocation.

quote_json: "directly contains the data of the struct"
requirement: A variable of struct type contains the struct's data directly.
A variable of class type contains a reference to the object's data.
The language's simple types are struct types.
A struct_declaration is a type declaration introducing a new struct type.
A struct declaration uses optional attributes, modifiers, ref and partial before struct and its name, then optional type parameters, interfaces and constraints, a body and an optional semicolon.
The declaration's identifier names the struct type.
A struct declaration cannot supply type-parameter constraints without a type-parameter list.

quote_json: "supplies a type_parameter_list is a generic struct declaration"
requirement: A struct with its own type-parameter list is generic.

quote_json: "struct nested inside a generic class declaration"
requirement: A struct nested within a generic class is itself generic.

quote_json: "generic struct declaration is itself a generic struct declaration"
requirement: A struct nested within a generic struct is itself generic.

quote_json: "type arguments for the containing type shall be supplied"
requirement: A constructed nested struct type requires the containing generic type's arguments.
A ref struct declaration cannot include a struct_interfaces specification.
A struct declaration may contain a sequence of struct modifiers.
The struct_modifier grammar admits new.
The struct_modifier grammar admits public.
The struct_modifier grammar admits protected where the declaration context permits it.
The struct_modifier grammar admits internal.
The struct_modifier grammar admits private.
The struct_modifier grammar admits readonly.
The struct_modifier grammar admits unsafe_modifier in unsafe code.
The unsafe_modifier form requires an unsafe context.
A struct declaration cannot repeat a modifier.

quote_json: "same meaning as those of a class declaration"
requirement: Struct modifiers other than readonly have the corresponding class-modifier meanings.
A readonly struct declaration declares immutable instances.

quote_json: "Each of its instance fields shall also be declared readonly"
requirement: A readonly struct cannot declare a non-readonly instance field.

quote_json: "None of its instance properties shall have a set_accessor_declaration"
requirement: A readonly struct cannot declare an instance property setter.
A readonly struct cannot declare a field-like event.
notes: The standard does not qualify this restriction as instance-only; see the clause question. Source pointers: 15.8.2.

quote_json: "its this is treated like an in argument/parameter"
requirement: The this of a readonly struct instance passed to a method is treated as an in parameter.

quote_json: "disallows write access to any instance fields"
requirement: That readonly this does not permit writes to instance fields outside constructors.
Constructors may write the readonly struct's instance fields.

quote_json: "instances are allocated on the execution stack"
requirement: A ref struct instance is allocated on the execution stack.
The ref modifier classifies the declared type as a ref struct.
A ref struct may contain ref-like fields.
notes: Ref-like does not by itself authorize ref field declarations; the closing note in 16.4.12.8 says ref fields are not valid in this edition. Source pointers: 16.4.12.

quote_json: "may not be copied out of its safe-context"
requirement: A ref struct value cannot be copied beyond its safe-context.

quote_json: "As the element type of an array."
requirement: An array cannot have a ref struct element type.
A class cannot declare a field of ref struct type.

quote_json: "a struct that does not have the ref modifier"
requirement: A struct without ref cannot declare a field of ref struct type.
A ref struct value cannot be boxed to System.ValueType.
A ref struct value cannot be boxed to System.Object.
A ref struct cannot be used as a type argument.

quote_json: "As the type of a tuple element."
requirement: A tuple element cannot have ref struct type.
A ref struct type cannot be used in an async method.
notes: The bullet omits a grammatical description of the use; scope is recorded as an open wording question.

requirement: A ref struct type cannot be used in an iterator.
notes: The bullet omits a grammatical description of the use; scope is recorded as an open wording question.

quote_json: "no conversion from a ref struct type to the type object"
requirement: No conversion exists from a ref struct type to object.
No conversion exists from a ref struct type to System.ValueType.

quote_json: "shall not be declared to implement any interface"
requirement: A ref struct cannot declare that it implements an interface.

quote_json: "not overridden in a ref struct type shall not be called"
requirement: An object or System.ValueType instance method not overridden by the ref struct cannot be called with a receiver of that ref struct type.

quote_json: "shall not be captured by method group conversion"
requirement: A ref struct instance method cannot be captured by a method-group conversion to a delegate.

quote_json: "shall not be captured by a lambda expression"
requirement: A lambda cannot capture a ref struct value.
A local function cannot capture a ref struct value.
The partial modifier classifies the struct declaration as a partial type declaration.
Partial struct declarations with the same name in the same enclosing namespace or type combine according to 15.2.7.
A struct_interfaces specification makes the struct directly implement its listed interfaces.
Each interface of a constructed struct is obtained by substituting the corresponding type arguments, including for types nested within generics.
A struct_interfaces specification consists of a colon and an interface_type_list.
A struct body's member declarations define its members.
A struct body encloses zero or more struct member declarations in braces.
A struct's members include the members introduced by its member declarations.
A struct's members include the members inherited from System.ValueType.
A constant declaration is a struct member declaration.
A field declaration is a struct member declaration.
A method declaration is a struct member declaration.
A property declaration is a struct member declaration.
An event declaration is a struct member declaration.
An indexer declaration is a struct member declaration.
An operator declaration is a struct member declaration.
An instance constructor declaration is a struct member declaration.
A static constructor declaration is a struct member declaration.
A type declaration is a struct member declaration.
A fixed-size buffer declaration is a struct member declaration in unsafe code.
A struct's fixed-size buffer declaration requires unsafe code.
Struct members follow the class-member descriptions in 15.3 through 15.12 subject to the differences in 16.4.
notes: This adopts the referenced rules without copying their predicates into clause 16. Source pointers: 16.4, 15.3, 15.12.

requirement: A struct cannot declare a finalizer.
Classes have reference semantics.

quote_json: "a compile-time error for A to depend on B"
requirement: If struct B has an instance field of struct type A, A cannot depend on B or a type constructed from B.

quote_json: "X contains an instance field of type Y"
requirement: A struct directly depends on another struct when it has an instance field of that type.
A struct's complete dependency set is the transitive closure of direct field dependencies.
Struct variables have independent data copies except for in, out and ref parameter variables.

quote_json: "not possible for operations on one to affect the other"
requirement: Updating one independent struct variable's stored value does not change another independent struct variable's stored value.
notes: This concerns the struct values themselves; the following marked note discusses shared referenced objects without adding a separate rule. Source pointers: 8.3.12.

quote_json: "two variables to reference the same object"
requirement: Class variables may alias one object so an operation through one can affect the object referenced by another.

quote_json: "not possible for values of a struct type to be null"
requirement: A non-nullable struct value cannot be null.
Every struct type implicitly inherits from System.ValueType.
System.ValueType inherits from object.

quote_json: "may specify a list of implemented interfaces"
requirement: An ordinary struct declaration may list implemented interfaces.

quote_json: "not possible for a struct declaration to specify a base class"
requirement: A struct declaration cannot specify a base class.
Struct types are never abstract.
Struct types are implicitly sealed.
A struct declaration cannot include the abstract modifier.
A struct declaration cannot include the sealed modifier.
A struct member cannot have protected declared accessibility.
A struct member cannot have private protected declared accessibility.
A struct member cannot have protected internal declared accessibility.
A struct function member cannot be abstract.
A struct function member cannot be virtual.
A struct can use override only for methods inherited from System.ValueType.

quote_json: "creates a copy of the value being assigned"
requirement: Assignment to a struct variable copies the assigned value.

quote_json: "copies the reference but not the object"
requirement: Assignment to a class variable copies the reference without copying the object.
Passing a struct as a value argument creates a struct copy.

quote_json: "returned as the result of a function member"
requirement: Returning a struct as a function-member result creates a struct copy.

quote_json: "using an in, out, or ref parameter"
requirement: A struct can be passed by reference using an in parameter.

quote_json: "using an in, out, or ref parameter"
requirement: A struct can be passed by reference using an out parameter.

quote_json: "using an in, out, or ref parameter"
requirement: A struct can be passed by reference using a ref parameter.
A struct property assignment requires its receiver expression to be a variable rather than a value.

quote_json: "classified as a value, a compile-time error occurs"
requirement: A struct indexer assignment requires its receiver expression to be a variable rather than a value.

quote_json: "all value type fields to their default value"
requirement: A struct's default value initializes each value-type field to that field's default value.
A struct's default value initializes each reference-type field to null.
The default value of a class or other reference-type variable is null.
A struct's default value is the value returned by its default constructor.

quote_json: "every struct implicitly has a parameterless instance constructor"
requirement: Every struct implicitly has a parameterless instance constructor returning the all-default field value.

quote_json: "treating the reference as another type at compile-time"
requirement: Converting a class value to object or an implemented interface preserves the reference.
A successful conversion from object or an interface back to a class preserves the reference.
Converting from object or an interface back to a class requires a runtime type check.
Converting a struct value to a reference type designated by 10.2.9 performs boxing.
Converting a designated reference value back to a struct according to 10.3.7 performs unboxing.

quote_json: "boxing and unboxing copies the struct value"
requirement: Boxing copies the struct value into the boxed instance.

quote_json: "into or out of the boxed instance"
requirement: Unboxing copies the struct value out of the boxed instance.
Invoking a struct's override of a System.ValueType virtual method through a struct instance does not box the receiver.

quote_json: "invocation occurs through an instance of the type parameter type"
requirement: Invoking that override through an instance of a type-parameter type does not box the struct receiver.
Accessing a constrained type parameter's member implemented within the value type does not implicitly box the receiver.

quote_json: "called with a reference to the variable"
requirement: A constrained interface-method implementation on a value type is called with a reference to the receiver variable rather than a boxed copy.

quote_json: "does not permit instance field declarations to include variable initializers"
requirement: A struct instance field declaration cannot include a variable initializer.

quote_json: "Static fields of a struct are permitted to include variable initializers"
requirement: A struct static field may have a variable initializer.

quote_json: "not permitted to declare a parameterless instance constructor"
requirement: A struct cannot explicitly declare a parameterless instance constructor.
A struct may declare an instance constructor with parameters.
A struct instance constructor cannot have a base constructor initializer, with or without arguments.

quote_json: "corresponds to an out parameter of the struct type"
requirement: The this parameter of a struct instance constructor is an out parameter of the struct type.

quote_json: "definitely assigned (\u00a79.4) at every location where the constructor returns"
requirement: A struct instance constructor cannot return without this being definitely assigned.
A struct constructor cannot read this explicitly or implicitly before definite assignment.

quote_json: "definite assignment to this that occurs prior to the body"
requirement: A struct constructor initializer definitely assigns this before the constructor body.
A struct constructor body following a constructor initializer has no remaining initialization requirement.

quote_json: "first of the following events to occur within an application domain"
requirement: A struct's static constructor is triggered by the first qualifying event in the application domain.

quote_json: "A static member of the struct type is referenced."
requirement: Referencing a static member is a qualifying trigger for the struct's static constructor.

quote_json: "An explicitly declared constructor of the struct type is called."
requirement: Calling an explicitly declared struct constructor is a qualifying trigger for the static constructor.
A struct auto-property uses a hidden backing field.
A struct auto-property's hidden backing field cannot be accessed outside its property accessors.

quote_json: "safe for the value to escape to"
requirement: Every expression has a compile-time safe-context enclosing it into which its value and fields may safely escape.

quote_json: "not a ref struct has a safe-context of caller-context"
requirement: An expression whose compile-time type is not a ref struct has caller-context safe-context.
A default expression of any type has caller-context safe-context.

quote_json: "an error if S2 is a wider context than S1"
requirement: Assignment cannot copy a source value into a destination with a wider safe-context than the source.
The possible safe-context values are declaration-block, function-member and caller-context, as for ref-safe-context.
A return statement's returned expression must have caller-context safe-context.

quote_json: "no argument (including the receiver) may have a narrower safe-context"
requirement: If a method invocation has a ref struct ref argument, every argument including its receiver must have a safe-context at least as wide as that argument's safe-context.
notes: A non-readonly ref struct receiver is included in the triggering arguments.

quote_json: "ref or out argument of a ref struct type"
requirement: If a method invocation has a ref struct out argument, every argument including its receiver must have a safe-context at least as wide as that argument's safe-context.

quote_json: "including the receiver unless the type is readonly"
requirement: If a method invocation has a non-readonly ref struct receiver, every argument including that receiver must have a safe-context at least as wide as the receiver's safe-context.

quote_json: "including the this parameter of an instance method"
requirement: A formal parameter of ref struct type, including instance-method this, has caller-context safe-context.

quote_json: "same as the safe-context of the foreach loop\u2019s expression"
requirement: A ref struct foreach iteration variable has the loop expression's safe-context.

quote_json: "same as the safe-context of that initializer"
requirement: A ref struct local other than a foreach iteration variable with an initializer has its initializer's safe-context.

quote_json: "variable is uninitialized at the point of declaration"
requirement: A ref struct local with neither a foreach iteration binding nor an initializer is uninitialized at its declaration.
A ref struct local with neither a foreach iteration binding nor an initializer has caller-context safe-context.
A field access e.F of ref struct type has the receiver e's safe-context.
A user-defined operator's safe-context is determined as for a method invocation.

quote_json: "narrowest context among the safe-contexts of the operands"
requirement: A value-producing operator's result has the narrowest safe-context among its operands.
A value-producing unary operator's result has its operand's safe-context.
A method or property invocation result has the smallest safe-context among caller-context and all argument expressions, including its receiver.
notes: The list components are accounted for in the following coverage blocks.

requirement: A property get invocation uses the underlying accessor method's safe-context rules.
A property set invocation uses the underlying accessor method's safe-context rules.
A stackalloc result has function-member safe-context.
A constructor new expression follows the invocation safe-context rules as though a method returned the constructed type.
With an object initializer, the constructor result's safe-context is additionally limited by the smallest safe-context among all arguments and all operands of its initializer expressions recursively.

quote_json: "Except for the differences noted in \u00a718.3, the descriptions of class members provided in \u00a717.2 through"
requirement: The class static-constructor triggers apply to structs without a default-construction exception. Executing new S() for a struct triggers its static constructor before the new instance is returned.
notes: See coverage.tsv for the mapped text block.

requirement: A record struct declaration creates a value type derived from System.ValueType, retaining struct copying and boxing semantics.
notes: This block covers readonly, non-positional record structs; positional members and struct with expressions are outside it. See also draft-v8 struct value semantics and alpha-v13 structs 16.5.

requirement: A record struct implements IEquatable of its own type, with interface calls dispatched to its strongly typed Equals member, whether synthesized or explicitly declared.
notes: This block covers readonly, non-positional record structs; positional members and struct with expressions are outside it. See also draft-v8 struct value semantics and alpha-v13 structs 16.5.

quote_json: "unless a member with a \"matching\" signature is declared"
requirement: An explicit member with a matching signature suppresses only that record struct's corresponding synthesized member; other synthesized members remain available.
notes: This block covers readonly, non-positional record structs; positional members and struct with expressions are outside it. See also draft-v8 struct value semantics and alpha-v13 structs 16.5.

quote_json: "Object creation invokes the parameterless constructor if public"
requirement: Object creation of a struct with a public explicit parameterless instance constructor executes that constructor once, preserving its assigned values, effects and thrown exceptions.
notes: This block covers explicit parameterless constructors, not instance field initializers. See also draft-v8 structs default/constructor restrictions and alpha-v13 structs 16.8.9. Tests use assigned fields at C#10; C#11 auto-default struct analysis is not this feature. The primary's record-struct delegation paragraph is read with record-structs.md L234's primary-constructor condition, not as an unconditional restriction on non-positional declarations.

requirement: An explicit parameterless struct instance constructor must have public accessibility.
notes: This block covers explicit parameterless constructors, not instance field initializers. See also draft-v8 structs default/constructor restrictions and alpha-v13 structs 16.8.9. Tests use assigned fields at C#10; C#11 auto-default struct analysis is not this feature. The primary's record-struct delegation paragraph is read with record-structs.md L234's primary-constructor condition, not as an unconditional restriction on non-positional declarations.

requirement: A default expression for a struct zero-initializes its instance fields without executing its explicit parameterless constructor.
notes: This block covers explicit parameterless constructors, not instance field initializers. See also draft-v8 structs default/constructor restrictions and alpha-v13 structs 16.8.9. Tests use assigned fields at C#10; C#11 auto-default struct analysis is not this feature. The primary's record-struct delegation paragraph is read with record-structs.md L234's primary-constructor condition, not as an unconditional restriction on non-positional declarations.

requirement: Allocating an array of a struct initializes every element to zeroed fields without executing the element type's explicit parameterless constructor.
notes: This block covers explicit parameterless constructors, not instance field initializers. See also draft-v8 structs default/constructor restrictions and alpha-v13 structs 16.8.9. Tests use assigned fields at C#10; C#11 auto-default struct analysis is not this feature. The primary's record-struct delegation paragraph is read with record-structs.md L234's primary-constructor condition, not as an unconditional restriction on non-positional declarations.

requirement: Generic new T() with a new() or struct constraint executes the public explicit parameterless constructor of its struct instantiation on the registered dotnet target.
notes: This block covers explicit parameterless constructors, not instance field initializers. See also draft-v8 structs default/constructor restrictions and alpha-v13 structs 16.8.9. Tests use assigned fields at C#10; C#11 auto-default struct analysis is not this feature. The primary's record-struct delegation paragraph is read with record-structs.md L234's primary-constructor condition, not as an unconditional restriction on non-positional declarations.

requirement: A public explicit parameterless struct constructor emitted into a referenced assembly remains callable through object creation by the consumer.
notes: This block covers explicit parameterless constructors, not instance field initializers. See also draft-v8 structs default/constructor restrictions and alpha-v13 structs 16.8.9. Tests use assigned fields at C#10; C#11 auto-default struct analysis is not this feature. The primary's record-struct delegation paragraph is read with record-structs.md L234's primary-constructor condition, not as an unconditional restriction on non-positional declarations.

quote_json: "An instance member of the struct is referenced."
requirement: The first reference to an instance member of a struct triggers its static constructor if no earlier qualifying event does so.

quote_json: "An explicitly declared constructor of the struct is called."
requirement: Creating a default struct value alone does not trigger its static constructor; the constructor trigger requires an explicitly declared constructor.
notes: The closed trigger list also includes instance-member and static-member reference in 18.3.10, p. 271 (PDF p. 287).
